title: Systems toxicology unravels multi-tiered carcinogenic networks of zearalenone in gastric cancer.
summary: An integrated toxicology analysis identified 157 shared zearalenone and gastric-cancer targets; eleven machine-learning algorithms selected six candidate genes. Docking and molecular-dynamics analyses were followed by gastric-cancer cell assays, which supported altered proliferation and migration in vitro. These data do not establish carcinogenicity in humans or in-vivo causal effects.
ai_technology: Eleven machine-learning algorithms screened shared disease and chemical-target genes to select six candidate driver genes; computational pathway and binding analyses were followed by in-vitro cell experiments.

evidence.tested: The primary abstract and Results report 157 common zearalenone and gastric-cancer targets, six machine-learning-selected genes with reported AUC above 0.85, docking and 100-ns molecular-dynamics analyses, and in-vitro MKN-45 cell assays showing increased proliferation and migration at the tested low-concentration conditions. The experimental evidence is cellular and in vitro.
evidence.unknown: The cell assays are in-vitro evidence only; human gastric carcinogenicity and in-vivo causal effects were not established.
